title: Unified Hosted Endpoint Productization: PRD, Acceptance Criteria & Go/No-Go Playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Consolidate PRD and launch playbook covering the hosted endpoint surface: chat, completions, embeddings, and reranker endpoints. Goal is a single source of truth that captures product requirements, strict acceptance criteria, cross-team rollout checklist, and go/no-go gating for GA. This ticket coordinates product scope decisions, acceptance tests, and a minimal viable launch checklist so Engineering, Docs, DX, Security, and Sales have clear deliverables and timelines.
goals: Define explicit acceptance criteria for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank hosted endpoints
Align runtime SLOs, cost guardrails, and default model mappings for GA
Provide a concrete launch checklist with owners for docs, SDKs, tests, telemetry, billing, and canary
Minimize customer regression risk by locking required evals and rollout policies before GA
success_metrics: Latency P95 within target for each endpoint by region (region-specific targets attached)
Error rate < 0.5% at 99th percentile of traffic during canary
First-week usage meets internal adoption threshold (>= internal trial customers with >1000 tokens/day)
No critical security or compliance findings blocking GA
scope_included: API surface parity for hosted chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints
Default model catalog mapping and migration guidance for customers using legacy endpoints
Telemetry and per-route cost/latency breakdown in Console for the new endpoints
SDK updates for streaming and structured output primitives
Acceptance-level end-to-end tests and performance benchmarks
out_of_scope: Dedicated capacity product changes (Reserved GPU pools) beyond API compatibility
Large-scale model training or model onboarding beyond curated catalog
On-prem private deployment packaging changes for this timeframe
Major refactor of billing meter (only mapping to existing metering expected)
requirements: REST and SDK parity: same query parameters and response semantics for new endpoint names
Streaming support for chat and completions with incremental tokens and final event markers
Embeddings API returns deterministic vectors and includes metadata for model, version, and liked normalization
Reranker endpoint supports batch inputs and returns stable scores with tie-breaking deterministic ordering
Console: per-model latency and cost breakdown visible within 24 hours of traffic
Backwards-compatible request routing and compatibility header for legacy clients
acceptance_criteria: Each endpoint has an automated integration test exercising happy path, error handling, and rate limit behavior
Performance: P95 latency targets met in CI performance harness under representative QPS for each region
Quality: run canonical prompt set for chat/completions and ensure no regression beyond threshold (mean quality delta < 2%)
Observability: traces and token-level cost attribution appear in Console for all launch customers
Security: SSO, API key gating, and KMS integration smoke tests pass; security review signed off
Docs: Quickstart, Migration guide, and API reference published and linked from Console
SDKs: Node and Python SDKs include new endpoint wrappers and streaming samples in smoke tests
Billing: usage shows correct metering for tokens/embeddings/reranker units in staging export

open_questions: Default model mapping: should generative-completions default to low-cost quantized model or higher-quality variant for GA? (tradeoff: cost vs quality)
Embedding normalization: do we commit to L2-normalized vectors by default or provide an opt-in flag?
Reranker semantics: what is the canonical tie-breaking rule for equal scores across items?
Rate limits: do we expose separate per-endpoint rate limits at GA or apply unified token limits?
risks_mitigations: Risk: Canary uncovers model quality regression — Mitigation: automatic fallback policy to previous model variant + throttle new requests
Risk: Overspending from mis-metered embeddings — Mitigation: staging billing export validation and delayed invoice holds for first week
Risk: Console telemetry gap — Mitigation: ship observability with feature flag and validate on first 24h of internal traffic
Risk: SDK streaming edge cases — Mitigation: include streaming contract tests in CI and add explicit backpressure examples in docs
notes: This ticket is intentionally prescriptive for the GA surface while leaving room for runtime teams to choose kernel/quantization knobs. The product decision to ship conservative defaults (higher quality model) versus aggressive cost-savings default must be finalized by 2026-03-18. Coordinate closely with Applied ML to ensure evaluation harnesses are representative of enterprise workloads.
